events.title: Domain Events
events.parkedToastDescription: {{ids}} — stopped retrying after repeated failures. Nothing behind the cursor is being handled, and the log cannot be pruned past it.
events.forgetDescriptionWithLag: This deletes the cursor row, abandoning the {{lag}} event(s) it has not handled. They will never be delivered to it. If the consumer is re-registered it restarts wherever its code declares — which for most consumers means treating everything now in the log as already delivered. Use this for a consumer no process owns any more, not to unstick a working one.
events.forgetDescriptionNoLag: This deletes the cursor row. The consumer is up to date, so nothing is lost today, but a re-registered consumer restarts wherever its code declares rather than where this cursor sat.
events.eventTypesDescription: The catalog an extension can subscribe to. A type absent here is a type nothing in this instance publishes.

consumerDialog.descAbandoned: Retention gave up waiting for this consumer. Its backlog is forfeit — resuming it will not bring the skipped events back.
consumerDialog.descParked: Parked after repeated failures. It will not retry on its own until you resume it or skip the event it is stuck on.
consumerDialog.descRetrying: Still retrying. The cursor has not moved past the event below.

consumersTable.abandonedTitle: Retention gave up waiting: this backlog is forfeit and the consumer must be re-registered
consumersTable.parkedTitle: Stopped retrying after repeated failures — resume it, or skip the event it is stuck on
consumersTable.polledHereTitle: This process registers the consumer and polls it
consumersTable.polledElsewhereTitle: Registered in another process — the jobs worker, for the relay and the webhook dispatcher. The usual reading, not a fault.
consumersTable.emptyMessage: No consumer has a cursor yet
consumersTable.emptyDescription: A cursor row appears the first time a consumer runs.

webhooks.title: Webhooks

form.description: Deliveries are sent in event order, at least once, and a receiver should dedupe on the X-Cascadia-Event-Id header.
form.urlHelp: Must be a public address. Private, loopback and link-local targets are refused, and redirects are never followed.
form.programHelp: A scoped subscription receives only the events it can attribute to that program. A change order whose designs span programs is heard only by subscriptions for every program.
form.eventTypesHelp: Select none to receive every type, including types added by a future release.
form.signDeliveriesHelp: Recommended. Creation is refused when the instance has no ENCRYPTION_KEY, rather than storing a signing key in the clear.
form.allowInsecureHelp: Only for a receiver inside your own network. The body and its signature are both visible in transit.

table.autoDisabledTitle: Switched off automatically after repeated failures
table.allTypesTitle: Every type, including ones a future release adds
table.unsignedTitle: Deliveries are sent unsigned — the receiver cannot verify them
table.emptyDescription: Create one to deliver domain events to an external system.

confirm.rotateDescription: The current secret stops working immediately. Every delivery signed with it will fail verification until the receiver has the new one, and the new secret is shown only once.
confirm.deleteDescription: The subscription stops matching events immediately and its signing secret becomes unusable. Deliveries still queued are expired rather than sent. Its delivery history stays readable until retention prunes it.

secret.description: Copy this secret now. It is stored encrypted and is never shown again — a lost secret is rotated, not recovered.
secret.copyFailed: Copying to the clipboard failed. Select the secret above and copy it by hand before closing this.
secret.rotatedWarning: The previous secret stopped working immediately. Deliveries signed with it will fail verification until the receiver is updated.
secret.createdWarning: Give this to the receiver so it can verify deliveries. Every request carries an X-Cascadia-Signature header of the form t=<timestamp>,v1=<hmac>, an HMAC-SHA256 over v1.<timestamp>.<body> using the exact bytes received.

deliveries.title: Delivery log — {{name}}
deliveries.description: Newest first. Deliveries go out in event order within a subscription, so a failure holds the line until it succeeds or runs out of attempts.
deliveries.statusDeadTitle: Exhausted its attempts. The event was never delivered, and the log row is the record of that.
deliveries.statusExpiredTitle: Dropped rather than sent: older than the maximum pending age when the pump reached it, or still queued when the subscription was deleted.
deliveries.footerAll: That is every delivery still on record. Settled deliveries are pruned once they pass the retention period.

webhooks.dispatcherNeverRan: No jobs worker has run the webhook dispatcher on this instance yet.
webhooks.dispatcherLag: The webhook dispatcher has not moved since {{when}} and is {{lag}} events behind.
webhooks.startJobsWorker: Webhooks are sent by the jobs worker, not the web server, so start one.
webhooks.disabledDetail: Nothing is being delivered to {{names}} — the receiver failed repeatedly, or answered 410 Gone. Fix the endpoint, then enable it again.

form.editDescription: Scope changes take effect on the next request. The secret is unchanged — use Rotate to replace it.

policy.title: Expiration policy
policy.description: Applied when a key is issued. Changing it never shortens a key already in the field — revoke those explicitly.
policy.defaultLifetimeHelp: Used when a key is created without an explicit expiry. Blank means no default.
policy.maxLifetimeHelp: Requests beyond this are rejected, not silently clamped. Blank means no ceiling.
policy.requireExpiryHelp: Reject key creation that would produce a key that never expires.
